page: Amazon Web Services r8i.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and integer operations. In benchmark testing, the CPU demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2111.0 and a top-tier text processing score of 2958.0. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 8639.03 and a Passmark CPU score of 15566.59, reflecting its 4 physical core topology.

The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 639.13 GB/sec and an uncached large block write bandwidth of 46.27 GB/sec. Database operations, measured via Passmark, score at 4393.8, while Redis SET operations reach 15.16 million operations per second. For language model tasks, the instance handles small 135M model prompt processing at 991.53 tokens per second, but performance drops to a weak 8.69 tokens per second for 7B model text generation, highlighting a limitation for larger local inference workloads.

From a resource density perspective, the r8i.2xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound applications that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage. The lack of bundled local storage and the baseline network speed of 4 Gbps represent key tradeoffs, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent data. This profile is configured for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, and text processing pipelines.
